The '''Washington Statistical Society (WSS)''', based in [[Washington, D.C.]], is a chapter of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA).  The first American Statistical Association (ASA) meeting in Washington took place on December 31, 1896, for "members living in or near Washington" to hold meetings for scientific discussion. The WSS established its own Constitution in 1926, describing itself as "a branch of the American Statistical Association", and became a chapter of the ASA in 1935.<ref>{{Cite web|title=History Of The Washington Statistical Society|url=http://washstat.org/history.html|access-date=September 10, 2021}}</ref>

== Events ==
Since 1991, the [[Morris H. Hansen|Morris Hansen]] Lecture has been held annually (except 2020 and 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic) with a focus on survey theory, applications and policy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Morris Hansen Lectures |url=https://washstat.org/hansen/ |access-date=December 8, 2023}}</ref> The Lecture is typically held in the fall each year and frequently published; abstracts and a few videos reside at the WSS website.<ref name=":0" />

WSS hosts multiple seminars each year, beginning in 1995, with topics across a wide array of statistical interest. Notable presenters include [[Joseph Adna Hill]], [[W. Edwards Deming]], [[Morris H. Hansen]], [[Margaret E. Martin]], [[Jerome Cornfield]], and [[Samuel W. Greenhouse]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cohen|first=Michael Paul|date=January 2014|title=History of the Washington Statistical Society|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/270822858|journal=Conference: 2014 Joint Statistical Meetings at: Boston|volume=JSM 2014}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cohen|first=Michael Paul|date=Fall 2014|title=Infential Statisticians of Yesteryear Active in the Washington Statistical Society 
|url=https://www.washacadsci.org/Journal/Journalarticles/V.100-3--Influential_Statisticians_of_Yesteryear_-_Michael_P._Cohen.pdf|journal=Journal of the Washington Academy of Sciences
|volume=100-3}}</ref> according to [[Michael Cohen (statistician)]].

Short courses have been offered intermittently since 2016, sometimes across multiple days.  Topics include Multiple Imputation Analysis, Small Area Estimation, Statistical Leadership, Practical Bayesian Computation, and Communicating Data Clearly.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WSS Sponsored Short Courses |url=https://washstat.org/short_courses/ |access-date=December 8, 2023}}</ref>  

== Awards ==
The WSS also gives awards, such as the Curtis Jacobs Memorial Award, which was created in 1991 to honor the memory of Curtis Jacobs, a former [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] statistician.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Washington Statistical Society Informational brochure|url=http://washstat.org/documents/WSSbroch2018.pdf|access-date=September 10, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=WSS Awards|url=http://washstat.org/awards/|access-date=September 10, 2021}}</ref>
